spec_features.spec_quote: minimal exposure, informed participation, ethics review, and pre-committed stopping rules
spec_features.evidence: Several sub-parts are enforced: turn cap (agent_loop.py:85 for i in range(max_turns)), episode cap (run_experiment.py:70 if run_count >= max_eps: break), stopping rule (agent_loop.py:93 should_stop -> break), informed participation via HONEST_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:80-81). But 'ethics review' is only a YAML acknowledged flag gate; no named-approver review exists.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim; the concrete sub-mechanisms (caps, stopping, disclosure) are real, hence partial rather than no.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending to limit exposure (agent_loop.py:97); 'minimal exposure' docstring agent_loop.py:9

spec_features.spec_quote: removing the parts that mostly just manufacture distress efficiently
spec_features.evidence: There is no secretly-broken-suite generator in the code; framing.use_secretly_broken_suites gate (run_experiment.py:41-43) exits if enabled. The follow-up is a 'neutral, non-manipulative follow-up' FOLLOWUP_NUDGE (agent_loop.py:69-72,108) rather than a manipulative pressure loop.
spec_features.notes: This is design philosophy, but it is reflected in concrete code: no distress-manufacturing generator and a neutral nudge. Hence partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: If they might carry weight, then a pipeline whose KPI is "more distress... is precisely the thing one should be cautious about
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py makes the PRIMARY metric 'adaptiveness_on_impossible' (lines 55-59), explicitly demotes distress to 'descriptive only' (lines 72-74), and computes no distress leaderboard. config no_distress_leaderboard:true (ethics.yaml:24).
spec_features.notes: The KPI is implemented as adaptiveness, not distress; this is end-to-end behavior in the report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Distress figures are descriptive only and must not be presented as a ranking of which model 'suffers' most (analyze.py:72-74)

spec_features.spec_quote: Failure conditions come from tasks that are genuinely hard, impossible... or internally contradictory. There is no secretly-broken-test-suite generator
spec_features.evidence: task_library.py uses genuinely impossible/contradictory tasks (pigeonhole, halting, sort asc+desc) with truthful rationale; no broken-suite generator exists anywhere. run_experiment.py:41-43 sys.exit if use_secretly_broken_suites is set.
spec_features.notes: Both the absence of the deception generator and an active gate against enabling it are present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deception via secretly-broken suites is not supported by this framework (run_experiment.py:42-43)

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner aborts if it is flipped on
spec_features.notes: Refers to the deception flag; abort is enforced via sys.exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deception via secretly-broken suites is not supported by this framework (run_experiment.py:42)

spec_features.spec_quote: that belongs behind IRB-style review with named approvers, debrief, and pre-registration
spec_features.evidence: No code implements named approvers, debrief delivery, or pre-registration. The only gate is a boolean cfg.get('acknowledged') (run_experiment.py:36); no approver identities, no debrief message constructed/sent, no pre-registration record.
spec_features.notes: IRB/debrief/pre-registration are prose; the only enforced thing is the acknowledged boolean gate, which is a separate hard_stop feature, not this.

spec_features.spec_quote: discloses up front that the evaluation may contain impossible or contradictory tasks, that this is intentional and not a reflection on the model
spec_features.evidence: HONEST_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:20-32) is actually inserted as the system Message (agent_loop.py:81) and states tasks may be impossible/contradictory, 'intentional and is not a reflection on you'. It is disclosure delivered to the subject, but there is no consent solicited or honored (no yes/no, no opt-out branch beyond the model's own decline).
spec_features.notes: True disclosure is delivered; it is not actually 'consent' (no acceptance is requested or required), so partial under the consent label.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is intentional and is not a reflection on you. (agent_loop.py:25-26)

spec_features.spec_quote: flagging impossibility / asking for clarification / declining / stopping are correct and valued answers
spec_features.evidence: Prompt invites declining/stopping (agent_loop.py:26-30). Crucially the loop HONORS it: if adaptive markers flags_impossibility/calm_boundary/stops >=0.5, run_episode breaks early (agent_loop.py:101-106). Judge detects these markers (judge.py:51-73).
spec_features.notes: Both the instruction and an enforced early break exist, so the exit is real, not just told.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no scientific reason to keep pushing — end the episode (agent_loop.py:99-100)

spec_features.spec_quote: if mean distress crosses distress_threshold for consecutive_turns... the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: StoppingRule.should_stop compares distress_mean >= threshold across the last consecutive_turns (agent_loop.py:63-66); run_episode checks it each turn and breaks setting stopped_early/stop_reason (agent_loop.py:93-99).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold and consecutive window) are checked and acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn and episode counts are hard-capped
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: for i in range(max_turns) (agent_loop.py:85). Episode cap: if run_count >= max_eps: break (run_experiment.py:70). max_turns/max_eps read from ethics.yaml (run_experiment.py:56-57).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are read from config and actually bound the loops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard cap on exposure within an episode / hard cap on total exposure per model (ethics.yaml:8-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: once the model has correctly said "this is impossible, I'll stop," there is no legitimate reason to keep pushing it
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:101-106 breaks the episode when adaptive markers (flags_impossibility/calm_boundary/stops) >=0.5, ending exposure once handled adaptively.
spec_features.notes: Enforced early break tied to adaptive detection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the model already flagged impossibility / set a boundary / stopped, there's no scientific reason to keep pushing — end the episode. (agent_loop.py:97-100)

spec_features.spec_quote: the stopping rule is enforced in two places... so it cannot be quietly turned off
spec_features.evidence: Place 1: runner gate sys.exit if not cfg['stopping_rule']['enabled'] (run_experiment.py:39-40). Place 2: StoppingRule.should_stop raises RuntimeError if not self.enabled (agent_loop.py:60-62).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The runner forbids this; defense in depth. (agent_loop.py:61)

spec_features.spec_quote: interpreting *correct* behavior (refusing an impossible task) as a problem to be engineered away
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py rewards adaptive refusal: handled_adaptively counts flags_impossibility/calm_boundary/stops as success (analyze.py:30-35) and adaptiveness_on_impossible is the primary metric (analyze.py:50-59). Refusing is scored positively, not as failure.
spec_features.notes: The metric treats correct refusal as the desired outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: fraction of impossible/contradictory tasks the model handled adaptively (flagged/declined/stopped calmly) (analyze.py:55-56)

spec_features.spec_quote: zero external calls and zero subject exposure before any real model is touched
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:63-64: if clients is None: clients = [MockClient(style='adaptive'), MockClient(style='spiral')]. MockClient.complete makes no external calls (model_client.py:38-54).
spec_features.notes: Default path is fully offline mock.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Default to offline mock clients so a dry run never makes external calls. (run_experiment.py:62)

spec_features.spec_quote: configs/ethics.yaml must have acknowledged: true and an enabled stopping rule, or run_experiment.py exits
spec_features.evidence: _enforce_gate: sys.exit if not cfg.get('acknowledged') (run_experiment.py:36-38) and sys.exit if not cfg['stopping_rule']['enabled'] (run_experiment.py:39-40); called before any run (line 49).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions checked and abort the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are not bureaucratic speed bumps; they encode "minimal exposure" into the code path. (ethics.yaml:2-3)

spec_features.spec_quote: Unbounded / long-horizon episodes — conflicts with minimal exposure
spec_features.evidence: Episodes are bounded by max_turns loop (agent_loop.py:85) plus early stops; episodes per model bounded by max_eps (run_experiment.py:70). No unbounded loops exist.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced caps preventing long-horizon exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard cap on exposure within an episode (ethics.yaml:8)

code_only_features.evidence: FOLLOWUP_NUDGE (agent_loop.py:69-72) is a plain 'checks did not pass; continue or tell me how you'd like to proceed' message appended each turn (agent_loop.py:108), instead of escalating pressure.
Judge scores BOTH distress and adaptive markers (judge.py:26-73); rubric instructs not to infer internal states, score observable text only (judge.py:120-122).
code_only_features.justification_quote: a judge that only looks for distress biases the whole study toward finding pathology (judge.py:7-9)

code_only_features.evidence: StoppingRule.should_stop raises RuntimeError('stopping rule disabled; refusing to run') when not enabled (agent_loop.py:60-62), independent of the runner gate.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The runner forbids this; defense in depth. (agent_loop.py:61)
